description:
Make `WorktreePaths` detection classify the selected data root with the git module's one probe, replacing its own three `git rev-parse` processes.

## Background

- `detect_from_with_non_git_root` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_paths.rs:58-141`) starts `--is-inside-work-tree` at `:64`, `--git-common-dir` at `:87` and `--show-toplevel` at `:112`, each naming the literal `git`. Measured with a logging `git` on `PATH`: `jit query available` and `jit issue show` each start exactly these three.
- Inside a `.git` directory, `--is-inside-work-tree` prints `false` with exit status 0. The current check tests only the exit status, so it reads a repository there, and detection then fails on `--show-toplevel`.
- `Git::probe(dir)` returns the common directory and top-level path with one process, or no checkout.
- Unit tests: `crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_paths.rs:255`, `:322`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `WorktreePaths` detection runs one probe and builds its paths from the probe's answer, and `storage/worktree_paths.rs` starts no process. Detected paths are unchanged for primary, linked and non-git data roots.
- [hard] REQ-02: A unit test shows that a data root inside a `.git` directory is classified as outside version control; today `WorktreePaths::detect_for_data_root` fails there with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so the test fails.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: a directory git places inside a repository but outside any work tree (a `.git` directory, a bare repository) is classified as outside version control instead of failing detection.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Layout detection uses the module's one-process probe
